- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 7–10 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.6–1.0) correlate with price corrections; if sentiment rises sharply, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to account for volatility decay.
